clue.text: Author's regularly choosing macabre volume in secrecy

definitions.note: the clue says 'the author is', meaning the setter of this puzzle, who signs as this pseudonym

indicators.note: regularly choosing means taking every other letter of the word macabre
in places the volume abbreviation inside the word for secrecy

parts.note: to keep someone in the dark is to keep a secret from them, so dark stands for secrecy

explanation.surface: A writer is quietly picking out a grim old tome to read in private.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly choosing' takes the even letters of the grim adjective. The definition is the setter's own pseudonym: Aardvark, who wrote this puzzle, names himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Aardvark is the pen name of the setter who wrote this crossword, so he is the author referred to.

clue.text: Martial art one child displayed in centre of Laos

indicators.note: in places the person pieces inside the central pair of letters
centre of here takes the inner letters of the country name Laos, dropping its first and last

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
a kid is an informal word for a child

explanation.surface: A youngster is seen performing a fighting discipline in the heart of a South-East Asian country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displayed' is just surface; 'in' does the placing, with 'centre of' keeping the two inner letters of the country name.
explanation.definitionFit: Aikido is a Japanese discipline of self-defence that uses throws and locks, so it is an example of a martial art.

clue.text: Change title of poem — an error's shown up

indicators.note: shown up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone wants a poem retitled because a mistake in it has been exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'shown up' means read upwards: EMANER runs across 'poem — an error's', and read from the bottom up it gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something a different name is to change its title, so the two phrases are synonyms.

clue.text: Mitt briefly lifted by a runner abroad

indicators.note: in a down clue lifted means the shortened word is read from the bottom up
briefly says the synonym for mitt is cut short by losing its final letter

parts.note: a mitt is a kind of glove

explanation.surface: A baseball glove is carried briefly by an athlete competing overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops the last letter of the glove word, and 'lifted' reads it upwards in this down clue. 'runner' means a river here, not an athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: The Volga is Russia's great river, and a river is a runner in crossword language because it flows; abroad marks it as foreign.

clue.text: Delia, broadcasting, goes through lines in a willing manner

indicators.note: goes through means the scrambled name passes between the letters for lines

parts.note: RY, short for railway, stands for lines of track

indicators.note: broadcasting suggests scattering seed widely, so the name Delia is scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A TV cook, while presenting her show, runs through her script eagerly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcasting' rearranges the name, and 'goes through' sets the result between the two railway letters. Delia Smith is a well-known British TV cook, which gives the surface its picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something readily means doing it willingly and without hesitation, so the adverbs match.

clue.text: Slate flooring

definitions.meaning: to slate someone is to criticise them harshly, like hauling an employee in for a dressing-down
a covering laid over a floor, such as a woven rug fitted wall to wall

explanation.surface: A roofing stone being used as a floor covering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slate' looks like roofing material, but here it is a verb meaning to tell someone off.
explanation.definitionFit: To be called in and told off is to be reprimanded; a fitted floor covering of woven fabric is the second sense.

clue.text: Legendary hero daring male to punch soon

indicators.note: to punch means to force a way into, so the pieces go inside the word for soon

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon
game means willing or daring, as in game for anything

explanation.surface: A brave man of myth is ready to throw a punch before long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daring' is an adjective, game as in game for anything; 'to punch' sends it and the male letter into the old word for soon after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon was the king of Mycenae who led the Greeks at Troy, a hero of Greek legend.

clue.text: Education department boosted in the past government year

indicators.note: boosted means lifted up, which in a down clue reads the abbreviation from the bottom up

parts.note: DEP is an abbreviation for department
ago means in the past, as in long ago

explanation.surface: Schools policy: a ministry once given more money by the administration that year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boosted' turns DEP upwards to PED, which starts the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedagogy is the method and practice of teaching, the theory of education.

clue.text: English flower at home beginning to develop exotic fruit

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Tamar is an English river between Devon and Cornwall
in means at home, as in staying in

indicators.note: beginning to takes just the opening letter of the word develop

explanation.surface: An English bloom kept indoors starts to grow into something from the tropics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' means a river: the Tamar is the river dividing the English counties of Devon and Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: The tamarind is a tropical tree whose sour pods are eaten, a fruit foreign to Britain.

clue.text: Blood left to permeate dress — it's a tragedy

parts.note: blood means family, kin, as in blood relations

indicators.note: to permeate means to spread through, so the abbreviation for left goes inside the word for dress

parts.note: gear means clothes, what one wears

explanation.surface: Blood soaking through clothing is a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to permeate' places L inside GEAR, after the G.
explanation.definitionFit: King Lear is one of Shakespeare's great tragedies, about an old king and his daughters.

clue.text: Ill-planned sprawling manor houses deserted

indicators.note: houses means holds inside, so the scrambled word contains the abbreviation
sprawling means spread out untidily, so the letters of manor are laid out in a new order

explanation.surface: A badly designed country estate, sprawling, with houses standing empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sprawling' makes RANOM from MANOR, and 'houses' puts D inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something random is done without a plan or method, haphazard.

clue.text: Poles switched annual break

parts.note: S and N stand for the south and north poles

indicators.note: switched means turned round, so the abbreviation for annual is read the other way

parts.note: PA, short for per annum, means yearly

explanation.surface: Polish people swapped their yearly holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' means compass points, not people from Poland. 'switched' turns PA to AP.
explanation.definitionFit: To snap is to break suddenly with a crack, as a twig does.

clue.text: Curse brown bananas, past peak — all should be returned

indicators.note: all should be returned says every piece is read backwards, the whole string reversed
past means going beyond, so the colour and the madness come after the top-of-the-charts piece

parts.note: NO I reads as No. 1, number one, the peak of the charts
tan is a light brown colour
bananas is slang for mad, crazy

explanation.surface: Someone swears at fruit gone brown and overripe, wanting it all taken back to the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peak' is No. 1, top of the charts, written NO I; 'past' sets the colour and the slang for crazy after it, and 'all should be returned' reverses the whole string.
explanation.definitionFit: Damnation is used as an exclamation of anger, so it is a curse.

clue.text: Listener admits limits to learning composer

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the word for listener holds the edge letters

parts.note: an ear is the organ that listens

indicators.note: limits to means the boundary letters, the first and last of the word learning

explanation.surface: A good listener is open to the edges of knowledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limits to' keeps only the first and last letters of 'learning', and 'admits' sets them inside the organ of hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Elgar was an English composer, known for the Enigma Variations.

clue.text: Women look here for dairy product

parts.note: hey is a call for attention, like saying look here

explanation.surface: Females wanting milk products are told where to look.
explanation.definitionFit: Whey is the watery liquid left after milk curdles in cheese-making, a by-product of dairy.

clue.text: Fast food? One says "ja"

definitions.meaning: a quick snack of minced beef in a bun sold at takeaways
someone from the German city of Hamburg, who says ja, German for yes

explanation.surface: Asked whether they'd like takeaway, someone answers yes in German.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition names a citizen of Hamburg, a German speaker, who would say 'ja'.
explanation.definitionFit: A beef patty in a bun is classic fast food; an inhabitant of Hamburg in Germany also takes the name.

clue.text: Cocktail measure knocked back — family drinks gallons

indicators.note: knocked back means turned back, so the word for a measure is read in reverse

parts.note: a nip is a small measure of spirits

indicators.note: drinks means takes in, so the word for family holds the abbreviation

parts.note: kin means family, relatives

explanation.surface: A tot is downed in one, while the relatives put away gallons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking but reverses the small measure of spirits; 'drinks' then puts the gallon abbreviation inside the family word, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pink gin is gin flavoured with Angostura bitters, a traditional mixed drink.

clue.text: Represent Sweden, top class, losing mile

parts.note: S is the international vehicle code for Sweden
a peak is the top of something

indicators.note: losing means dropping, so the abbreviation for mile is taken out of the word for class

parts.note: a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A Swedish athlete of the highest class misses out on the mile race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top class' reads as one phrase meaning first-rate but splits into two synonyms; 'losing' takes the mile abbreviation from the school-class word.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak for someone is to act as their spokesperson, representing them.

clue.text: Greek character extracting one pound from an Italian — fiddler perhaps

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: extracting means pulling out, so the letters for one and pound are removed from the islander

parts.note: a Sicilian is an Italian from the island of Sicily
I is the Roman numeral one
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A Greek man takes a pound from an Italian, perhaps a cheat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extracting ... from' removes I and L from SICILIAN to leave SICIAN. 'fiddler' suggests a cheat but means a violinist.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiddler plays the violin, so he is an example of a person who plays music; perhaps marks the example.

clue.text: Satisfied following fruit drop

indicators.note: following means the word for satisfied comes after the fruit

parts.note: a plum is a fruit
met means satisfied, as in met the requirements

explanation.surface: Content after eating some fruit, someone lets it fall.
explanation.definitionFit: To plummet is to fall steeply, so drop is a synonym as a verb.

clue.text: Brassy thing having bath alfresco, principally

parts.note: a tub is a bath

indicators.note: principally means first of all, taking the opening letter of alfresco

explanation.surface: A brazen sort takes a bath in the open air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brassy' sounds like brazen but means made of brass.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuba is a large low brass instrument, so it is a brass object.

clue.text: Crouch End approached by secondary road

indicators.note: approached by means the abbreviation for a road comes just before the word end

parts.note: in Britain a B road is a secondary road, below an A road

explanation.surface: A suburb of north London, Crouch End, is reached by a minor road.
explanation.walkthrough: Crouch End is a district of north London, which hides the definition at the start. B roads are Britain's minor roads.
explanation.definitionFit: To bend down is to stoop or crouch, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Dodgy Malibu receives one complaint

indicators.note: receives means takes in, so the scrambled word holds the numeral
dodgy means unreliable or not right, so the letters of Malibu are put in a different order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A suspect bottle of coconut rum leads to someone grumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodgy' makes BULIMA from MALIBU, and 'receives' places I in it before the final A. Malibu is a brand of coconut rum.
explanation.definitionFit: Bulimia is an eating disorder, and complaint can mean an illness or medical condition.

clue.text: Fire station not right for party

indicators.note: not means without, so the abbreviation for right is removed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The fire station is not the right place for a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: FIRE plus STA gives FIRESTA, and 'not' removes the R.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiesta is a festive celebration, originally a Spanish religious holiday, so a party.

clue.text: Toilet occupied a long time going over cryptic

indicators.note: occupied means filled, so the toilet word sits inside the reversed time word
going over means turning over, so the word for a long time is read backwards

parts.note: an era is a long period of time
can is slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: The loo has been engaged for ages and someone is getting impatient over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going over' turns ERA to ARE, and 'occupied' means that word is filled by CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcane means mysterious, understood by few, so it is a synonym of cryptic.

clue.text: All the best gold coats fade

indicators.note: coats means covers, so the gold symbol is wrapped around the word for fade

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
to die away is to fade

explanation.surface: The finest gold leaf is losing its shine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All the best' looks like a phrase opening the clue, but it is a farewell; 'coats' wraps the gold symbol round the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is a farewell, and all the best is a phrase used when saying goodbye.

clue.text: Novel cooking pot — one full of porky pies?

parts.note: a billy, or billycan, is a camping cooking pot
porky pies is rhyming slang for lies, so someone full of them is a liar

explanation.surface: Is this new cooking pot one that's stuffed with pork pies?
explanation.walkthrough: Porky pies is British rhyming slang for lies; a pork pie is a cold British meat pie. 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Billy Liar is a 1959 novel by Keith Waterhouse about a daydreaming young man who tells lies.

clue.text: Agreed to accept voting system here in northern Europe

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so the word for agreed holds the voting system

parts.note: yes means agreed
PR, proportional representation, is a voting system

explanation.surface: A country somewhere in northern Europe agrees to adopt proportional representation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accept' sets the voting-system abbreviation inside the word of agreement, after its first letter. The definition is the town itself, 'here' in northern Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Ypres is a town in Flanders, Belgium, a place in northwest Europe famous for its First World War battles.

clue.text: Border gang seen in unoccupied France

indicators.note: seen in means the word for gang is placed inside the emptied country
unoccupied means emptied, so only the outer letters of France are kept

parts.note: a ring is a gang of criminals

explanation.surface: A gang crossing the border into the unoccupied zone of wartime France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unoccupied' empties the country name to its outer letters, and 'seen in' puts the gang between them. It recalls Vichy France, the unoccupied zone in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: A fringe is the edge or border of something, as in the fringes of a town.

clue.text: Gourmet food making doctor run out — incontinent?

clue.text: Exhaust from limousine attracts German and Yankee

indicators.note: attracts means draws in, so the car letters hold the German word

parts.note: RR, Rolls-Royce, stands for a luxury car
und is German for and
Yankee is the radio alphabet word for Y

explanation.surface: Fumes from a big car draw a German and an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German and' looks like a list but gives the German word for 'and'; 'attracts' places it inside the Rolls-Royce letters, with the Yankee letter after.
explanation.definitionFit: To run dry is to become used up, so exhaust here is a verb meaning to use up completely.

clue.text: George, in seat shivering, put on something woolly here in English resort

indicators.note: put on means placed after, so the woolly animal comes first

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep, which is woolly

indicators.note: in means George's letter is placed inside the scrambled seat
shivering means shaking, so the letters of seat are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: George, shivering in his seat at an English seaside resort, puts on a woolly jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shivering' makes SATE from SEAT, and 'in' puts G inside it to make SGATE. Ramsgate is a seaside resort town in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramsgate is a seaside town on the Kent coast, a holiday resort in England.
